name: Ping & Latency Test
description: Measure HTTP network round-trip latency, jitter, and connection stability to global server nodes in real time.
technology: HTML5 Fetch API / High Resolution Timers
userProblem: Users experiencing lag during gaming, video calls, or browsing need to diagnose whether network latency or connection jitter is the bottleneck.
searchIntent: Measure precise round-trip time (RTT) in milliseconds to major global CDNs and evaluate network stability for gaming and video meetings.
resultInterpretation: Under 30ms = Excellent (Competitive Gaming, Real-time audio). 30–70ms = Good (Smooth 4K streaming, Zoom calls). 70–150ms = Acceptable. >150ms = Noticeable lag. Jitter indicates connection consistency; jitter > 15ms causes voice stutters.
practicalGuidance: If ping is high or jitter is > 20ms, switch from 2.4GHz WiFi to 5GHz WiFi or a wired Ethernet cable. Check if background downloads or VPN routing are increasing latency.
limitations: Browser-based ping measures HTTP application-layer round-trip time via performance.now(). It includes TLS/TCP overhead and will be slightly higher than raw ICMP ping in command line terminal.
formula: Round Trip Time (RTT) = T_response - T_request; Jitter = Mean(|RTT_i - RTT_{i-1}|)
trustNotes: Lightweight client requests sent to public Anycast edge endpoints with zero tracking.

seo.metaDescription: Test your internet latency to major global cloud endpoints (Cloudflare, AWS, Google). Measure min, avg, max ping and jitter in milliseconds.

faqs.question: What is considered a good ping time?
faqs.answer: Under 30ms is excellent, 30-70ms is good for browsing and gaming, 70-150ms is acceptable, and over 150ms will feel noticeably laggy.

faqs.question: How is HTTP ping different from ICMP ping?
faqs.answer: Standard ICMP ping runs at the network layer, while browser HTTP ping measures full TCP + TLS + HTTP handshake roundtrip.
